senses.m: Merchandising: the process of selecting products to sell within limited shelf space and cash constraints
Shelf space: a limited retail resource used to display products
Assortment: the collection of products offered, defined by width and depth
Merchandise planning: determining the quantity of goods to purchase based on inventory and sales targets
Procurement/Buying: the process of sourcing goods from suppliers
Category: a specific group of related products (e.g., beverages, stationery)
Variety/SKU: specific items within a category
Width: the number of different product categories offered
Depth: the number of varieties offered within a single category
Inventory: goods held in stock for sale
Sales: the act of selling goods or the revenue generated
Cost price: the price at which a retailer buys goods from a supplier
Selling price: the price at which a retailer sells goods to customers
Gross margin: the percentage of profit calculated as (selling price - cost price) / selling price
Open-to-Buy (OTB): the budget limit for purchasing new inventory
Turnover: the speed at which inventory is sold and replaced
Traffic builder: low-margin items used to attract customers into the store
Profit generator: high-margin items that contribute significantly to store profit
Gross Margin Return on Investment: a metric measuring profit generated per unit of inventory cost
